channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Why Prompt Templates Break Silently After a Model Bump
item.description: Model version bumps rarely crash your pipeline. They just shift behaviour enough that your prompt template stops working the way you tested it.

item.title: What an Evaluation Harness Should Log Beyond the Score
item.description: A final score hides the interesting part of evaluation. I walk through what to log so you can actually trust and debug your numbers.

item.title: Grouped and Stratified Splits: Picking the Right One
item.description: A cross-validation scheme is only as honest as the assumptions behind it. Learn when to group, when to stratify, and when you need both at once.

item.title: Why Fine-Tuning Results Vary Run to Run, Honestly Reported
item.description: One fine-tuning run is an anecdote, not evidence. Here is where the noise comes from and how to report results you can actually trust.

item.title: Designing a Held-Out Test Set That Resembles Deployment
item.description: Most test sets are accidentally too easy. Here is a worked example showing how to build one that actually predicts deployment performance.

item.title: Red-Teaming Versus Standard Evaluation: Why You Need Both
item.description: Standard evaluation measures typical performance; red-teaming hunts for adversarial failure. Here's why neither alone is enough, with a worked example.

item.title: Choosing a Metric for Imbalanced Text Classification
item.description: Accuracy can look great on imbalanced data while the model quietly ignores the minority class. Here is how to pick a metric that won't fool you.

item.title: Why In-Domain Scores Overstate NLP Model Quality
item.description: High in-domain accuracy often hides fragile models. I walk through why out-of-distribution evaluation matters and how to build it into your pipeline.

item.title: What a Loss Curve Tells You That a Final Metric Cannot
item.description: A final metric is a verdict. A loss curve is the trial. Here is why I read the whole training trajectory before trusting any score.

item.title: Comparing NLP Pipelines Honestly: Paired Tests Over Leaderboards
item.description: One leaderboard score is not evidence. Here is how paired tests on the same examples reveal whether a pipeline improvement is real or noise.

item.title: Fine-Tuning a Small Transformer: What Actually Changes
item.description: A concrete walkthrough of fine-tuning a small transformer: what the weights do, why learning rate and freezing choices matter, and how to check it actually worked.

item.title: Design Your Evaluation Protocol Before You Train Anything
item.description: Write your evaluation protocol before any training code exists. It is the single cheapest way to stop a project from quietly lying to you.

item.title: Why Accuracy Alone Cannot Tell You a Model Is Production-Ready
item.description: High accuracy can mask a model that fails exactly where it matters most. A look at why production readiness needs more than one metric.

item.title: Statistical Power in ML: Why Sample Size Limits Conclusions
item.description: Your test set size decides what differences you can ever detect. Underpowered ML comparisons produce confident-sounding noise, not evidence.

item.title: Reading a Multi-Class Confusion Matrix Properly
item.description: A single accuracy number for a multi-class model can hide systematic, costly confusions between specific classes. Here is how to read the matrix properly.

item.title: Evaluating Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Classifiers Fairly
item.description: A prompted model beating your fine-tuned baseline often means your comparison is broken, not that prompting won. Here is how to check.

item.title: What Makes a Dataset Leak-Proof: A Checklist Before You Train
item.description: A practical checklist for catching data leakage before training, with a worked example showing how an innocent-looking split inflates accuracy.

item.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation vs Fine-Tuning: One Small Case
item.description: A concrete walk-through comparing RAG and fine-tuning on a small knowledge base, with realistic numbers and a practical decision rule.

item.title: Deep Learning Versus Machine Learning: A Grounded Answer
item.description: Deep learning is not a replacement for machine learning; it is one family within it, suited to some problems and poorly suited to others.

item.title: Data Science Internships: Reading Between the Lines
item.description: Not all data science internships are equal. Here is how to spot the ones that will actually teach you something, before you waste a cover letter.
